note: Every profile here is synthetic - an illustrative composite of commonly reported notes for the region/process/roast combination, not a real cupped lot or a published score sheet. PLAN.md section 5's content bar: real profiles get synthetic:false and a citation in `source`; these are marked honestly until roaster-sourced score sheets replace them (STRATEGY.md section 5, the bag-QR loop). The Cause & Effect UI never hides the flag.

profiles.name: Ethiopia Yirgacheffe, washed
profiles.source: Composite of commonly reported washed-Yirgacheffe cupping notes (jasmine, black tea, lemon, honey) - not a specific lot.

profiles.name: Ethiopia Guji, natural
profiles.source: Composite of typical natural-Ethiopia notes: heavy berry fruit plus a mild fermented edge, which is the sun-dried process working as intended rather than a flaw - the deliberate pairing with `defect: "contextual"` in wheel.json (see DefectFlag in domain/types.ts).

profiles.name: Colombia Huila, washed
profiles.source: Composite of commonly reported Huila notes: red apple and malic brightness over a caramel/chocolate base - not a specific lot.

profiles.name: Brazil Cerrado, natural
profiles.source: Composite of the low-acid, nutty/chocolate profile typically reported for natural-process Brazils used in espresso blends - not a specific lot.

profiles.name: Costa Rica Tarrazú, honey
profiles.source: Composite illustrating the honey-process signature: the sugar-sweetness and syrupy body honey processing is chosen for, layered onto a washed-Costa-Rica citrus base - not a specific lot.

profiles.name: Sumatra Mandheling, wet-hulled
profiles.source: Composite of the low-acid, heavy-bodied, herbal/earthy profile commonly attributed to Sumatra's wet-hulled (giling basah) process and dark roasting - not a specific lot.

profiles.name: Kenya Nyeri, washed
profiles.source: Composite of the intense berry acidity and winey character Kenyan SL28/SL34 lots are commonly reported for - not a specific lot.

profiles.name: Panama Boquete, anaerobic natural
profiles.source: Composite illustrating an anaerobic-natural's boozy, tropical-fruit signature - the sealed-tank fermentation that defines the process pushed to the front - not a specific lot.
